A 55-year-old woman is admitted for open reduction surgery of a right femur fracture sustained in a
motor vehicle accident 2 hours ago. She has a 12-year history of rheumatoid arthritis and was
hospitalized a month ago for a flare, during which her prednisone dose was increased. Her current
medications include calcium supplements, methotrexate, and etanercept. She reports adequate
nutrition and regular medical follow-ups. Vital signs are stable, and cardiovascular examination is
unremarkable. To minimize the risk of post-operative wound healing complications, which adjustment
to her medication regimen is most appropriate? Answer Choices: (A) Starting low-dose aspirin to
improve vascular integrity (B) Switching from methotrexate to leflunomide temporarily (C) Discontinuing
steroids before surgery (D) Administering a single dose of IV methylprednisolone preoperatively (E)
Adding zinc supplementation (F) Replacing prednisone with hydrocortisone (G) Reducing prednisone
dose to the lowest possible level before surgery (H) Adding vitamin C supplementation to enhance
wound healing (I) Discontinuing etanercept to reduce the risk of infection (J) Increasing prednisone
dose initially and tapering rapidly after 3 days
 A. Adding zinc supplementation
B. Replacing prednisone with hydrocortisone
C. Switching from methotrexate to leflunomide temporarily
D. Increasing prednisone dose initially and tapering rapidly after 3 days
E. Reducing prednisone dose to the lowest possible level before surgery
F. Discontinuing steroids before surgery
G. Starting low-dose aspirin to improve vascular integrity
H. Adding vitamin C supplementation to enhance wound healing
I. Discontinuing etanercept to reduce the risk of infection
J. Administering a single dose of IV methylprednisolone preoperatively
